previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, and chronic heart failure, was admitted due to an episode of hypotension with generalized weakness. He had inadvertently restarted spironolactone and furosemide contrary to prior discharge instructions, leading to low blood pressure. Upon evaluation, his cardiac enzymes were negative, ECG and chest X-ray were unremarkable, and no acute cardiac or pulmonary issues were found. His symptoms resolved with discontinuation of the diuretics. He remained hemodynamically stable throughout the stay, with blood pressure in the 110s to 130s. Medication adjustments were made, including holding furosemide and spironolactone until cardiology follow-up, reducing atorvastatin and metoprolol doses, and continuing all other chronic therapies. He was discharged home with clear instructions on medication management, diet, weight monitoring, and urgent follow-up.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Chest pain, cough and weakness.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph, ___.

PA AND LATERAL VIEWS OF THE CHEST:  Low inspiratory lung volumes are again
noted.  The cardiac, mediastinal and hilar contours are unchanged.  The lungs
are clear without focal consolidation.  There is no pleural effusion or
pneumothorax.  No acute osseous abnormalities are present.

IMPRESSION:  No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality.

HISTORY:  Diabetes with CAD and cough and elevated white count, to evaluate
for pneumonia.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with the study of earlier in this date, there are
continued low lung volumes.  Some prominence of interstitial markings could
reflect mild elevation of pulmonary venous pressure.  No definite acute focal
pneumonia is appreciated.
